Tree retriever LANDS. Section-grained ingest (675 nodes vs 1854 chunks) beats Phase 0 flat hybrid on every metric except r@1 (where it ties): r@5 89.7% vs 75.9% (+13.8pp), MRR 0.753 vs 0.705, and is ~7x faster (374ms vs 2470ms). Composes additively with the lifted QueryExpander: tree+expander r@5=96.5% — best aggregate result. v1 deliberately skips auto-merge (parent promotion) — landed the simpler thing first per the bd decision rule. Auto-merge can come in a follow-up if a use case wants to give the model parent-section context instead of leaf sections. 15 new tests, 1869/1869 green. Numbers committed in retrieval_eval/baselines/phase0.json.

Table-shape lands with a massive win. Stock TabularStore + query_table tool + bench wiring deliver r@1/r@5/r@k = 100% vs Phase 0's 58.3%/66.7%/75% on the same fixture — a +33-41pp lift, in ~1ms. The bench cell (table_sql_oracle) uses fixture-supplied SQL to measure the architectural ceiling; NL→SQL generation is the agent's job at chat time via the production query_table tool, which interpolates registered table schemas into its description so the model has the grounded context without a separate list_tables round-trip. Read-tier gate enforced at the store (rejects non-SELECT, cross-table refs, unknown FROM targets). 31 new tests (21 store + 10 tool), 1900/1900 green, deterministic across reruns. Side win: surfaced a wrong expected_record_ids in the q_hard_oct_damaged fixture row — the table cell exposed the discrepancy that flat hybrid had been mirroring. The thesis from the data-retrieval-primitives notes is validated: tabular data needs to be retrieved AS tables.

Context Package + Contract Bundle land as the architectural shift the data-retrieval-primitives spike was building toward. RetrievalContextPackage wraps shape-aware retrieval in one envelope with intent / access (user_id scoping) / proof (per-hit provenance) / budget (token cap). ContractBundle declares per-role what each slot needs from which shaped store; assemble_package walks the contract, dispatches to episodic / tree / tabular, returns a complete or incomplete package. Required-slot misses surface in missing_required_slots so the agent gets told what's missing rather than working with silently-incomplete context. Worked end-to-end demo: retrieval_eval/contracts/returns_handler.yaml + test_contract_returns_handler.py pulls customer history (episodic) + refund policy (episodic) + matching orders (tabular) in one call, against the same synthetic returns CSV Phases 0-2 used. 34 new tests (13 package + 17 contract + 4 end-to-end), 1934/1934 green. Pure module — no model dependency, no I/O beyond the stores it's given. CLI/chat integration intentionally deferred — the primitive is ready for a caller (a tool that materializes a package, a per-role session-start renderer) when there's a use case.

AssembleContextTool ships. Wired into both REPL + TUI tool-registry builders, registered in the new 'contract' tool profile (plus 'full'). Tool spec interpolates every registered contract's role + template variables at construction so the model sees available contracts inline. Read-tier (no write-confirmation flow). Renders the package as markdown grouped by slot with provenance footnotes + missing-required-slot warnings. Tabular + tree store wiring deliberately deferred to harness-kgpi (returns-handler character) — the tool surfaces a clear error string for slots needing un-wired stores. 13 new tool tests + 1947/1947 green overall.
